definitions.explanation: An attractive quality suggesting sensuality or romantic appeal. Can describe both men and women.
A desire or aspiration for something, often used in the expression {色気|いろけ}を{出|だ}す (to show interest/ambition for something beyond one's usual scope).

examples.japanese: {色気|いろけ}のある{人|ひと}だ。
あの{俳優|はいゆう}は{大人|おとな}の{色気|いろけ}がある。
examples.english: That actor has a mature charm.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}のダンスには{色気|いろけ}があって、{観客|かんきゃく}を{魅了|みりょう}した。
examples.english: Her dancing had an allure that captivated the audience.

examples.japanese: {社長|しゃちょう}のポストに{色気|いろけ}を{出|だ}す。
examples.english: To show ambition for the company president position.

examples.japanese: {余計|よけい}な{色気|いろけ}を{出|だ}したせいで、かえって{失敗|しっぱい}してしまった。
examples.english: Because I got greedy and tried for too much, I ended up failing instead.

notes:
Composed of {色|いろ} (color, but also romantic/sexual connotation) and {気|け} (air, feeling). The word carries a range from subtle allure to overt sensuality depending on context.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {色気|いろけ}がある — to have sex appeal
- {色気|いろけ}を{出|だ}す — to show interest/ambition (sense 2); to try to be seductive (sense 1)
- {色気|いろけ}たっぷり — full of allure
- {大人|おとな}の{色気|いろけ} — mature charm
- {色気|いろけ}より{食|く}い{気|け} — appetite over romance (proverb)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {魅力|みりょく} — charm, attractiveness (broader, not necessarily sexual)
- セクシー — sexy (direct loanword, more casual)
- {艶|つや} — gloss, luster, also used for sensual beauty (literary)
